name: Truck terminal / truck parking
summary: Secured, paved tractor-trailer parking (and optionally a cross-dock terminal building) priced per truck space. Cost is mostly heavy-duty paving, grading and stormwater, plus fencing, lighting, gate/guard house and cameras; driver amenities, a cross-dock building or reefer plug-ins are add-ons. Public evidence is limited to FHWA benefit-cost case-study assumptions ($35k–$75k/space incl. land or amenities), so the baseline is a bottom-up derivation from the paving building block.

typicalSize.method: FHWA case studies use 60–100-space facilities (e1/e2/e4); private secured truck yards commonly 50–300 spaces (judgment).

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Gross paved SITE area per truck space (not building SF): 12×70–75 ft stall (~860 SF) + share of 60–75 ft maneuvering aisles and entry ≈ 1,600–2,400 SF.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Bottom-up: ~1,900 SF gross per space ≈ 211 SY, of which ~85% paved = 180 SY. Heavy-duty asphalt (thicker section than paving-block asphalt $45/SY → ~$55–$70/SY) to heavy-duty concrete ($85–$170/SY, paving block, mid $115) → $9.9k–$20.7k. + grading/drainage/detention $2k–$5k + perimeter fence, gate, high-mast lighting and CCTV share $2k–$4k ≈ $14k–$30k; mid ≈ asphalt/concrete mix $15k + $4k + $3k = $22k. High $35k adds concrete throughout, poor soils and a guard building. Cross-check: FHWA Phoenix low-cost facility $35k/space INCLUDING land (e2) and Portland $75k/space with driver amenities and public-project overheads (e1).

perSF.method: Per SF of gross paved site: perPrimaryUnit ÷ sfPerPrimaryUnit (14,000/1,750 ≈ 8; 22,000/1,900 ≈ 11.6; 35,000/2,300 ≈ 15).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P: clearing/grading, heavy-duty pavement and base, striping, storm drainage/detention, perimeter fence and gate, lighting, CCTV, small guard/office. Excludes cross-dock terminal building, driver amenity building, reefer plug-ins, parking-availability sensors (optional lines), land, soft costs, off-site road/signal work and fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy = low/mid (14/22; stabilized aggregate or thin asphalt); premium ≈ (mid+high)/2/mid (full concrete, guard house); luxury ≈ high/mid uplifted for amenitised public-style facility.

systemSplit.method: From the bottom-up mid: pavement + fence ≈ $12k (32), earthwork $3.3k (31), storm $1.8k (33), lighting $1.5k (26), cameras/gate controls $1.1k (28), guard-house footings 03, GC 8%. Judgment.

lineItems.name: Heavy-duty pavement per truck space (~180 SY)

cost.method: Low = heavy asphalt section (~$55/SY, above paving-block asphalt $45); mid $85 = asphalt/concrete mix; high = paving-block heavy-duty concrete high $170/SY.

lineItems.name: Entry gate, guard house and access control

cost.method: Judgment: prefabricated guard booth $25k–$80k + motorized gates/arms, card readers and intercom $25k–$170k.
NCDOT estimate $3,500 per space installed (e3); range ±(lot-size economies of scale noted in the same study).

lineItems.name: Driver restroom / amenity building (~800 SF)
lineItems.notes: Optional; drives the FHWA Portland case ($75k/space, e1).

cost.method: Judgment: 480V pedestal, conduit/trenching and share of service upgrade per equipped space. Quantity 25% of spaces.

lineItems.name: Cross-dock terminal building (per door, optional)

cost.method: Narrow (~100–120 ft) cross-dock with doors both sides at 12 ft centers ≈ 600–720 SF of building per door × $140–$220/SF (C&W small-building $144/SF as base, heavier slab/door density) + dock package ~$18k ≈ $100k–$200k per door. Quantity ≈ 0.4 doors per trailer space (2–3 trailer stalls per door).

lineItems.notes: Turn on for a terminal (LTL) project; the engine can report per door.

pctOfHard.method: Civil-only design, traffic study, stormwater permits, survey/geotech: 8–18% of hard cost (judgment).

softCosts.notes: Type-specific soft items: traffic impact study and driveway/curb-cut permits; zoning/conditional-use approval is often the critical path.

hard.method: Earthwork/soils and stormwater quantities dominate risk (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low × 1.05 for a gravel/asphalt yard; max ≈ concrete yard with guard house (high $35k) × 1.3 for soft and contingency; amenitised public facilities (FHWA $75k, e1) exceed this.

evidence.quote: The hypothetical project involves the construction of a 100-space parking facility that offers amenities to truck drivers. The project is assumed to have capital costs of $7.5 million
evidence.scopeNotes: FHWA benefit-cost case study (analysis dated 2021): $7.5M / 100 spaces = $75,000/space. Public facility with driver amenities; capital cost incl. planning/design; assumption, not a bid.

evidence.quote: repurposes a vacant lot … into a low-cost public truck parking facility with the capacity to accommodate 100 trucks … assumed to cost $3.5 million (including land acquisition and construction costs)
evidence.scopeNotes: $3.5M / 100 spaces = $35,000/space INCLUDING land; construction-only share not given. Assumption in an FHWA case study.

source.title: Truck Parking Study Phase II: Concepts of Operations (2020)

evidence.quote: A vehicle occupancy detection approach is based on an estimated cost of $3,500 for installation per truck parking space.
evidence.scopeNotes: Truck parking availability system (in-ground sensors) only; excludes electrical, paving.

evidence.quote: a staging area … that will handle up to 60 trucks at one time with included weight scales, restrooms, and refrigeration hookups … The cost of the new road and staging area is reported to be approximately $3 million.
evidence.scopeNotes: Combined new public road + 60-truck staging area with scales/restrooms/reefer hookups; ≤ $50,000 per truck space as an upper bound only.

openQuestions: Find a state DOT truck-parking project bid tab (per-space construction cost) to replace the derived baseline.
Cross-dock terminal per-door cost is derived; a public LTL terminal budget would firm it up.
